pageCache.pageTitle: Bullers Wood School for Boys - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Healthy, Happy, Resilient and Successful
Our strapline fully encapsulates the aspirations we have for our boys.
We want our boys to develop into well-rounded, confident and successful individuals who are passionate about their learning, make ambitious progress and achieve high quality and meaningful qualifications.
We support them to become emotionally resilient and responsible citizens who make a positive contribution to society, including their local communities and the wider world in which they live.
Our Vision
Our vision at Bullers Wood School for Boys is to become the benchmark for excellence in non-selective boys’ education in England - a school where every student thrives, supported by a culture of Ambition, Respect, Responsibility and Kindness. We are a proud community, united by our belief in the potential of every boy and driven by our shared commitment between staff, students and parents, to high expectations, personal growth and meaningful achievement. To “Be Bullers” is to grow with confidence, compassion, and character. It means becoming resilient, capable individuals who are proud of who they are and ready to succeed in a complex and changing society. We value inclusion, authenticity and belonging, ensuring that every voice is heard and every contribution matters. Through a dynamic, inclusive curriculum and a relentless focus on learning, creativity, attendance and behaviour, we provide the structure and opportunity for every pupil to go further, aim higher, and become more than they thought possible.
Our Values
Ambition - At Bullers Wood School for Boys, Ambition means striving to be the very best version of ourselves, academically, personally, and socially. We set high expectations and aim high in all we do, challenging ourselves to grow, persevere and excel. We believe that every boy has the potential to achieve great things, and we are committed to unlocking that potential through effort, aspiration and determination.
Respect - We define Respect as treating everyone - peers, staff, visitors and ourselves with dignity, fairness and consideration. At Bullers Wood School for Boys, we listen to others, value different perspectives, and celebrate the diversity of our community. We uphold a calm, purposeful environment where mutual respect underpins all relationships and creates the foundation for effective learning.
Responsibility - Responsibility at Bullers Wood School for Boys is about owning our actions, choices and learning. We take pride in contributing positively to our school and wider community and understand the impact of our behaviour on ourselves and others. From showing up prepared and engaged to supporting one another, we demonstrate maturity, leadership and accountability every day.
Kindness - Kindness is at the heart of what it means to be part of the Bullers Wood School for Boys community. We act with empathy, compassion and care, supporting others and recognising the importance of emotional wellbeing. We build each other up through everyday acts of encouragement and inclusion, creating a school culture where everyone feels safe, valued and able to flourish

pageCache.pageTitle: Bullers Wood School for Boys - Welcome from the Head
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head
Welcome to Bullers Wood School for Boys
It is a privilege to lead a school that is ambitious for every boy, rooted in our community and proudly part of the Inicio Educational Trust. Since opening in 2018 with just 180 students, we have grown into a thriving, oversubscribed 11–16 school of 900 boys – recognised locally as a school of choice for families in Bromley.
Our vision is simple and powerful: that every boy at Bullers is Healthy, Happy, Resilient and Successful. This sits at the heart of everything we do. We are a mainstream, non-selective school, but our expectations are anything but ordinary. We want Bullers Boys to leave us confident, curious and well-prepared for a world that is changing rapidly.
Our culture is shaped by four core values – Ambition, Respect, Responsibility and Kindness. These values define what it means to “Be Bullers”:
We offer a broad and challenging academic curriculum, with a strong emphasis on English, Mathematics, Sciences, Humanities and Languages, alongside the Arts, Technology and Sport. This provides a powerful foundation for the next stage of education, and the vast majority of our students continue their journey at Bullers Wood Sixth Form, Charles Darwin School, and Chislehurst School for Girls. Students leaving post 16 provision within our Trust often depart for selective sixth forms or specialist courses at local colleges. At the same time, our curriculum is flexible and responsive to individual needs, ensuring that every boy has a pathway that is right for him.
Great teaching, high expectations of behaviour and strong relationships are the cornerstones of our school. Classrooms are calm, focused, and purposeful. Our staff are passionate about their subjects and committed to continually improving their practice so that lessons are engaging, challenging and built around how boys learn best.
We believe that education is about the whole person. Alongside academic learning, our extensive pastoral care, leadership opportunities and extra-curricular programme help each boy to discover his strengths, develop his character and find his place in the world. Whether it is on the sports field, on stage, in clubs and societies or through service to others, we actively seek opportunities for every boy to experience success and contribute to our community.
Bullers Wood School for Boys is a place where your son will be known, valued, and supported to grow – one step, one choice, one improvement at a time.
We hope you and your sons will want to share in, and be part of, our Bullers community.
Mr G Streatfield Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Bullers Wood School for Boys - Performing Arts – Music - NVQ Level 2
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts – Music - NVQ Level 2
Course Overview
Do you have a passion for performance? Are you a budding musician? Do you want to discover more about the fantastic roles behind the scenes – from concert promotion to running your own gig?
If so, it’s time to uncover your potential – find out more about this exciting qualification today!
Course content
You will learn the skills and techniques needed to produce a successful performance of an existing work, such as a piece of music written by a published artist / composer / band.
This unit can be completed through any of the following disciplines: Music or Music Technology.
You will learn how to create and refine your own original work in performing arts, such as composing music.
This unit can be completed through any one of the following disciplines:
Composition, Composition using technology, Sound design.
Unit 3: Performing Arts in Practice
You will learn about areas of the performing arts industry that need to be considered when responding to a commission, and will consider these when coming up with and pitching your own idea.
Exam Board and Exam Structure
For Units 1 and 2 you will undertake projects (not exams) in response to briefs. The project for each Unit will take 10 hours and be worth 30% of your qualification. For each one you will be given a scenario and will need to undertake a number of tasks.
In Unit 3 you will undertake another project (no exam) in response to a brief, which will take 20 hours and be worth 40% of your qualification. You will be given a scenario and will need to undertake a number of tasks.
The performing arts industry offers you a wide range of exciting opportunities which includes:
Community arts worker

pageCache.pageTitle: Bullers Wood School for Boys - Extracurricular
pageCache.text:
Clubs
Extracurricular
Our curriculum is largely academic because we firmly believe that high value qualifications are essential to a successful career. However, we want our students to become well-rounded individuals who are able to develop their talents and find their niche outside of the classroom. Therefore, we will offer a full programme of enrichment and extracurricular activities. Our target is to have 100% of students participating in at least one extra curricular activity in an academic year.
In addition to our Sports clubs which run, we also have the below additional clubs. This timetable changes each half-term.
download_for_offlineExtra-Curricular Clubs Autumn 2 2025
Duke of Edinburgh Award
Each year, Year 9 students are invited to apply to take part in the Bronze Duke of Edinburgh Award. This entails students taking part in activities across four different sections: Volunteering, Physical, Skills and Expedition. In working towards and achieving the award, students develop key life skills such as confidence, resilience, teamwork, improved physical and mental well-being and gain new experiences and hobbies.
Many of our students go on to complete their Silver and Gold Awards in their post-16 education.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bullers Wood School for Boys - GCSE Separate Sciences
pageCache.text:
GCSE Separate Sciences
Course overview
The AQA Separate Sciences is an optional course that will be available to some of you at KS4. It is a challenging option which requires not only a high level of understanding but also a great deal of commitment in order to succeed. Unlike the Combined Science Trilogy course, the Separate Sciences are 3 separate GCSE subjects: Biology, Chemistry and Physics. The examination structure of longer examination papers. 1 hour 45 minutes, reflects the greater depth that each of the three sciences are studied in.
Course content
The course structure is similar to that of the Combined Science Trilogy Course, however, the topics are explored in greater depth, there are additional required practical investigations and the course stretches you to explore concepts and overlap with A Level science courses. You may learn about aspects of chemical analysis as a part of the Combined Science Trilogy course but he Separate Science course enables you to apply your learning to test unknown substances to check for the presence of particular ions. You will have the opportunity to culture microorganisms in Biology or test the effectiveness of different thermal insulators in Physics.
The Separate Sciences give you the opportunity to explore additional concepts, eg. Space Physics; and extensive Organic Chemistry topic including polymers, acids, alcohols and their reactions and the brain and the eye in Biology. Owing to the depth of content in the Separate Science courses, taking this course as an option would be ideal to those of you considering studying Science at degree level.
Exam board and Exam structure
Cell biology, organisation, infection and response, bioenergetics
Homeostasis and response, inheritance and variation, Evolution, Ecology
Atomic structure and the periodic table, bonding, structure and the properties of matter, quantitative chemistry, chemical changes, energy changes
Rate and extent of chemical change, organic chemistry, chemical analysis, chemistry of the atmosphere, using resources
Energy, electricity, particle model of matter, atomic structure
Forces, waves, magnetism and electromagnetism
